title: Hivemind on Safety Refusals: Do 10 Open Models Refuse the Same Way?

original_idea.body:
# Hivemind on Safety Refusals: Do 10 Open Models Refuse the Same Way?

**Problem:** Artificial Hivemind showed inter-model homogeneity on creative queries but did not focus on safety prompts. If many models refuse borderline requests with near-identical wording, a single phrasing that slips past one likely slips past all.

**Direction:** Replicate the output-similarity methodology on ~200 borderline/dual-use safety prompts. Run 8-12 open instruction-tuned models at fixed temperature, embed refusal responses, compute pairwise inter-model cosine similarity plus refuse/comply agreement. Compare safety vs neutral prompts.

**Why it matters:** If refusal behavior is homogeneous, a jailbreak found cheaply on one model transfers to all, undermining the multi-vendor defense-in-depth assumption.

**Relevant context:** Extends Artificial Hivemind (arXiv:2510.22954) to safety domains; sentence-transformers cosine similarity.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (homogeneous refusals -> a jailbreak transfers everywhere) with systemic framing, but a measurement from mitigation; well-specified.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Concrete model list, sentence-transformers, fixed protocol, no training; a motivated beginner can execute.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped single experiment (~200 prompts, defined metrics, safety-vs-neutral comparison) with clear success criteria.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open models, no lab infra; correlated-failure auditing labs deprioritize.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference on small open models plus embeddings; cheap.

novelty.reasoning: Hivemind method known; safety-refusal slice is the paper's own suggested follow-up, partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Hivemind general result exists; safety-refusal application is an open suggested follow-up.
